Montréal Finally Has a Terrace Map

Terrasse Season is a free, bilingual directory of 180 terraces, patios, and rooftops across Montréal, searchable by neighbourhood, type, and features. Ready for the 2026 season.

The Problem It Solves

Montréal's terrace scene is bigger than most people realize. Every publication has its own "best terraces" list, and they all cover roughly the same 15 to 20 headline spots. Read one and you've read them all. Nobody sits down and cross-references twelve of them to find everything else.

So people go back to the same two or three they already know. Not because those are the best, but because finding anything else takes more work than it should. Terrasse Season did that cross-referencing work once, so you don't have to.

What It Does

  • 180 terraces across 24 Montréal neighbourhoods, from Old Montréal to Ahuntsic to NDG
  • Interactive map with a browsable sidebar list — see the whole city at once, click any spot to explore
  • Filters by neighbourhood, terrace type (rooftop, patio, backyard), dog-friendly, covered, heated, and open right now
  • Sort by distance from your location
  • Live hours from Google Places, refreshed before each season
  • Bilingual — full English and French interface
  • Free, no account required

The Data

We cross-referenced 12 Montréal publications (Time Out, Tastet, Cult MTL, Tourisme Montréal, Narcity, Daily Hive, OpenTable, Montreal Diaries, MTL Blog, The Rooftop Guide, experienceoldmontreal.com, and Eater Montréal) and took everything mentioned across all of them, not just the headline picks. We added spots we know personally that didn't make it into any list. And we accept submissions from the public and from bar and restaurant owners, which we review before adding.

Features like covered, heated, and dog-friendly are only shown when a source actually confirms them. If something isn't listed, it means we don't have a confirmed source for it, not that the answer is no. Hours come from Google Places and get refreshed before each season.

Story Angles

  • "Montréal finally has a terrace map": the city has one of the best patio scenes in Canada and, until now, no single place to find all of it
  • Neighbourhood breakdown: which areas have the most rooftops, the most covered terraces, the most dog-friendly spots
  • Seasonal resource to share before the first warm weekend of the year
  • Bar and restaurant owners can submit their own terraces, and anyone can flag corrections
  • Bilingual from the start, for both communities

About Terrasse Season

Terrasse Season is a one-person project, built by a Montréaler for Montréalers. Listings come from editorial sources and are verified where possible. Anyone can suggest a missing terrace or flag a correction directly through the site.
